MISSION LOG - SV MERIDIAN

Day 1. Departure from Luna high dock proceeded on schedule. The helium-3 scoop
deployed cleanly at the first burn and telemetry shows collection efficiency at
97 percent. We committed to the Ceres transfer window at 0340; the next window
would have cost us nineteen days. Crew morale is high and the new galley is
already popular.

Day 3. First full systems review complete. All primary buses nominal. The
water reclaimer is running two points above its acceptance test numbers.

SYSTEMS

Day 7. The coolant manifold on the reactor loop shows a pressure drop of 12
percent against the departure baseline. Engineering traced it to a weeping seal
on junction C-4 and clamped it; pressure is stable but we will machine a
replacement seal before the return leg.

Day 9. The starboard thruster misfired twice during the correction burn. The
fault isolated to a sticky propellant valve; cycling it cleared the fault, but
the valve goes on the overhaul list. Port thruster performance remains nominal.

NAVIGATION

Day 12. The navigation gimbal shows a drift of 0.3 degrees accumulated since
departure, at the edge of tolerance. We recalibrated against the pulsar fix and
scheduled a quantum beacon calibration at relay buoy K-9, which we pass on day
15. Star tracker two was cleaned of a film deposit that was dimming magnitude
readings.

CREW

Day 16. The hydroponics bay produced its first full salad harvest, eleven
kilograms of greens, to general celebration. Doctor Ilse Marek reports the crew
fit, with radiation dosimetry well inside limits. The chess ladder has become
fiercely competitive; the chief engineer remains undefeated.

ARRIVAL

Day 22. Ceres approach and capture were textbook. Docking clamps engaged on the
first attempt at berth seven. The cargo manifest transfers 400 tonnes of
regolith processing equipment to the surface consortium; unloading begins at
first shift tomorrow. Return window analysis begins next week.
